posts.text: This week in immigration enforcement, the money and the paperwork tell the story. A death the government never announced, a medical billing system that stopped paying, and federal grants that reach only the police departments willing to partner with ICE. 🧵
posts.summary: Exposes ICE enforcement practices including unreported deaths and payment failures
posts.quote: This week in immigration enforcement, the money and the paperwork tell the story. A death the government never announced, a medical billing system that stopped paying, and federal grants that reach only the police departments willing to partner with ICE. 🧵

posts.text:
42

ICE was running about 42 AI tools internally as of May 2024 while listing only 23 in the federal inventory built to disclose them. It took litigation to surface the real count.

Records via Just Futures Law, Pangea Legal Services, and Mijente.

143

143 New York state and local officials have signed a letter asking Schumer and Jeffries to defund and dismantle ICE, up from 107 on July 20. The suburban and upstate names are what change the political math.

Reporting by City & State New York.

posts.text:
$3B

The Justice Department is offering roughly $3 billion for immigration enforcement through a program it named BIDEN. An agency qualifies only if it joins a 287(g) partnership with ICE or commits to entering one. A second round closes August 19.
posts.summary: Exposes Justice Department grant structure incentivizing ICE partnerships

249

ICE is seeking 249 parking spaces around Boston on a lease of at least three years, part of a solicitation covering more than a dozen cities. That lease describes a scale of local operations ICE has announced nowhere else.

Reporting by WBUR.

posts.text:
1,400

ICE plans to reopen Rivers Correctional Institution in North Carolina by year's end with 1,400 beds, one of the largest immigration jails on the East Coast. Rural placement puts distance between detained people and their lawyers.

Reporting by The Marshall Project.

$96M

The VA processed 233,772 medical, dental, and pharmacy claims for people in ICE and CBP custody over nine months of 2025. Providers have apparently gone unpaid for any care given since October 1.

Records obtained by American Oversight.
